title: Finding out what a pack really does before you install it

questions.q: When does top-level code in a pack's __init__.py run?
options: Every time ComfyUI starts, whether or not you use a node
Only when you add one of its nodes
Only when you update the pack
questions.answer: Every time ComfyUI starts, whether or not you use a node
questions.why: load_custom_node executes the module on import.
main.py runs it before the rest of ComfyUI starts.

questions.q: What is an honest result from reading a pack?
options: What you read, what you found, and what you didn't read
It has many stars, so it is fine
The README agrees with the code, so it is safe
questions.answer: What you read, what you found, and what you didn't read
questions.why: You can't prove safety from reading.

questions.q: Why not run Python from inside a pack's folder to inspect it?
options: A pack can plant files that shadow standard modules
questions.answer: A pack can plant files that shadow standard modules
questions.why: An interpreter looks in the script's folder first.

questions.q: A pack has a compiled .so file for its core logic. What do you note?
options: You can't read that part, so your review doesn't cover it
It is safer, because it is compiled
questions.answer: You can't read that part, so your review doesn't cover it
questions.why: It may have a normal reason, but your report must say what you didn't read.

questions.q: You read version 1.2, and the pack updates. What now?
options: Read the difference, because new commits are new code
questions.answer: Read the difference, because new commits are new code
questions.why: Pin what you read and review changes.
